posts.cooked:
While I do manage to get into a fair number of games with people, I have a recurring experience i don't understand.  VERY often -- usually several times each play session -- I find an open game with one person in it.  As soon as I enter the game, that person leaves.

 

It can be a game that just appeared a second ago, or one that I've watched sit open for a few minutes before joining.  So I doubt it's just my bad luck to enter as they decide to leave for unrelated reasons.  The factor that seems to trigger the other person leaving is my entry.  They never say anything.

 

I talked to some folks in a game and some of them said they'd had the same experience.  What the heck?  One guy said he leaves and re-enters to dodge holding the crown.  But in the encounters I am talking about, the departing player never returns.

 

Any clue what's going on?

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
Actually, the thing that really annoys me in online games is some of the etiquette. It's a little bit irritating when everybody is immediately suggesting what card they think should be played out of their turn instead of holding back for at least a few seconds to allow the other players to consider their options. I guess it's understandable when you realise people may have played a lot of solo games and are just used to clicking on the card they want to activate every turn, but then I've had a couple of games where people are also giving others a telling-off in the comments about making a choice against their wishes, or asking for turns to be rewound because they didn't like the outcome, which is just off.

On the subject of rewinding, I personally don't like to do it unless someone really borked their turn and wants to go back (I've done that myself before when I was away and rushed my turn in a panic when I got back), preferring to just roll with the punches instead of trying to craft the perfect game. I've thought about using the closed hands feature, but it's also important to know what cards the others have and without VOIP visible hands is the only effective way to communicate that.

I'm also annoyed with some of the brusqueness, when people are barking orders like "Advanced" or "Voss" or in the comments, and the head-on rush to get through games as quickly as possible. Playing SotM in person tends to be more relaxed, more chatting and discussion of strategy; even when we used to play on Google+ it was far more relaxed and sociable. It just seems that there are quite a few people in the online game circle who just want to rush through the games without any time for pleasantries, expecting everybody to play the game their way and without delay. It's not endemic or anything, but it's not the sort of table I'd join on a club night if you know what I mean, and yet I don't have much choice on whose game I get involved in.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
If I have a suggestion, I tend to just use the chat and explain my reasoning for it. Otherwise, I tend to trust that the other players have some idea what they're doing. I try not to second guess, but there was one time someone used Turmoil to put Hasten Doom on top of Bomber Blade's deck, which led to a chain of targets being played capped by Devious Disruption.

And I typically don't suggest a rewind unless someone's turn ended up being totally useless in a foreseeable way (i.e., using a low-damage card on someone who has enough DR to nullify it).

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked: I think the nature of how the game was made and released has created some interesting situations. When it was only a card game, you played with about the same people over and over. Those people have their own strategies and their groups have their own strategies. Over the years, those strategies become the "good play". Once multiplayer hit, and we are now seeing a bunch of different ways to play, some people are having a hard time differentiating between "good-bad plays" and "different approaches".

posts.name: morph147
posts.cooked:
Will have to second Pydro a bit. Only reason I do the suggestion thing is trying to see what different people try and share my strategy. Never expect anyone to use it. Good way to share strategy and teach newer players about the game and different ways to think about the decks. Now for selection of who to target, since it is a co-op game that should always be talked about a bit so the suggestion button just allows for quicker coomunication than just the chat. 

For example I play the scholor now completely different than I once did. I never used the forms, period. For me they were dead cards and scholor wasn't that great. Now because of multiplayer and different people sharing their strategies, I see how powerful scholor actually is and love playing him. 

Ultimately everyone has to remember it's a suggestion only. You don't have to follow it and play the deck the way you want. Just remember there are people who are trying to learn and don't be afraid to share the knowledge.
